study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modeling of brain morphometry in self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives: to quantify individual deviations from the normative range of brain morphometry in children with SeLECTS and to assess their associations with clinical manifestations and cognitive functions. It also provides research hypotheses regarding heterogeneity.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Our goal is to quantify individual deviations from the normative range of brain morphometric variation in children with Self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes and to assess their associations with clinical manifestations and cognitive functions. ... We hypothesized that children with SeLECTS would exhibit varying degrees of heterogeneity compared to the normal population.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses the devCCNP dataset as a reference cohort. It describes the eligibility criteria (typically developing, no history of neurological or psychiatric illness), specifies image quality standards (no gross abnormalities on brain MRI), and reports the final sample size (457). The original publication for the dataset is cited.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: This project enrolled typically developing school-age Chinese children and adolescents, and this study comprised 241 boys and 216 girls, aged 3 to 18 years, with a mean age of 10.44 ± 3.11 years. All normal participants had no history of neurological disorder or psychiatric illness and no gross abnormalities on brain MRI images. ... Full details for the devCCNP have been published (Fan et al. 2023).

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex were used as covariates in building the normative models. Site effects from the multi-site devCCNP data were addressed using ComBat-GAM harmonization.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Using age and sex as covariates, normative models for each regional morphometric measure were developed utilizing data from a multisite sample of 457 healthy individuals ... The optimal covariate combination included site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) (Pomponio et al. 2020) and the incorporation of intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, and mean surface area in the regional models

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: The normative deviation for each regional morphometric measure was defined as the z -scores ...
